{{short description|none}}
{{Differential equations}}

[[Differential equation]]s are prominent in many scientific areas. [[Nonlinear system|Nonlinear]] ones are of particular interest for their commonality in describing real-world systems and how much more difficult they are to solve compared to [[Linear system|linear]] differential equations. This list presents nonlinear [[ordinary differential equation]]s that have been named, sorted by area of interest.

|[[Darboux equation]]
|1
|<math>\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{P(x,y) + y R(x,y)}{Q(x,y) + xR(x,y)}</math>
|A generalization of the [[Jacobi equation]]. Can be solved without quadratures, if certain amount of distinct particular solutions are found. In case <math>P\left(x, y \right)</math> and <math>Q\left(x, y \right)</math> are [[Homogeneous polynomial|homogenous polynomials]] of the same degree, this equation is either [[Homogeneous differential equation|homogenous]] itself, or can be reduced to a [[Bernoulli differential equation]].
|<ref>{{Cite web |title=Darboux equation - Encyclopedia of Mathematics |url=https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Darboux_equation |access-date=2024-06-02 |website=encyclopediaofmath.org}}</ref>

|[[Lorenz attractor]]
|1
|<math>\begin{align}
\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} &= \sigma (y - x) \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} &= x (\rho - z) - y \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}t} &= x y - \beta z
\end{align}</math>
|[[Chaos theory]], [[dynamical system]]s, [[meteorology]]
|<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lorenz |first=Edward N. |date=1 March 1963 |title=Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow |url=http://journals.ametsoc.org/doi/10.1175/1520-0469(1963)0202.0.CO;2 |journal=Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences |language=en |volume=20 |issue=2 |pages=130–141 |doi=10.1175/1520-0469(1963)020<0130:DNF>2.0.CO;2 |bibcode=1963JAtS...20..130L |issn=0022-4928}}</ref>

|[[Nahm equations]]
|1
|<math>\begin{align}
\frac{dT_1}{dz}&=[T_2,T_3]\\
\frac{dT_2}{dz}&=[T_3,T_1]\\
\frac{dT_3}{dz}&=[T_1,T_2]
\end{align}</math>
|[[Differential geometry]], [[gauge theory]], [[mathematical physics]], [[magnetic monopole]]s
|<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Donaldson |first=S. |[[Painlevé transcendents|Painlevé I transcendent]]
|2
|<math>\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = 6 y^2 +  t</math>
|One of fifty classes of differential equation of the form <math>y'' = R(y', y, t)</math>; the six Painlevé transcendents required new [[special functions]] to solve
|<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Painlevé-type equations - Encyclopedia of Mathematics |url=https://encyclopediaofmath.org/index.php?title=Painlev%C3%A9-type_equations |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=encyclopediaofmath.org}}</ref>
|-
|[[Painlevé transcendents|Painlevé II transcendent]]
|2
|<math>\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = 2 y^3 + ty + \alpha</math>
|One of fifty classes of differential equation of the form <math>y'' = R(y', y, t)</math>; the six Painlevé transcendents required new [[special functions]] to solve
|<ref name=":2" />
|-
|[[Painlevé transcendents|Painlevé III transcendent]]
|2
|<math>ty\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = t \left(\frac{dy}{dt} \right)^2-y\frac{dy}{dt} + \delta t + \beta y + \alpha y^3 + \gamma ty^4</math>
|One of fifty classes of differential equation of the form <math>y'' = R(y', y, t)</math>; the six Painlevé transcendents required new [[special functions]] to solve
|<ref name=":2" />
|-
|[[Painlevé transcendents|Painlevé IV transcendent]]
|2
|<math>y\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}=\tfrac12 \left(\frac{dy}{dt} \right)^2+\beta+2(t^2-\alpha)y^2+4ty^3+\tfrac32y^4</math>
|One of fifty classes of differential equation of the form <math>y'' = R(y', y, t)</math>; the six Painlevé transcendents required new [[special functions]] to solve
|<ref name=":2" />
|-
|[[Painlevé transcendents|Painlevé V transcendent]]
|2
|<math>\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}=\left(\frac{1}{2 y }+\frac{1}{ y -1}\right) \left( \frac{dy}{dt} \right)^2
-\frac{1}{t} \frac{dy}{dt}+\frac{( y -1)^2}{t^2}\left(\alpha y +\frac{\beta}{ y }\right) +\gamma\frac{ y }{t}+\delta\frac{ y ( y +1)}{ y -1}</math>
|One of fifty classes of differential equation of the form <math>y'' = R(y', y, t)</math>; the six Painlevé transcendents required new [[special functions]] to solve
|<ref name=":2" />
|-
|[[Painlevé transcendents|Painlevé VI transcendent]]
|2
|<math>\begin{align}
\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{y-1}+\frac{1}{y-t}\right)\left( \frac{dy}{dt} \right)^2-\left(\frac{1}{t}+\frac{1}{t-1}+\frac{1}{y-t}\right)\frac{dy}{dt}  \\
&+\frac{y(y-1)(y-t)}{t^2(t-1)^2} \left(\alpha+\beta\frac{t}{y^2}+\gamma\frac{t-1}{(y-1)^2}+\delta\frac{t(t-1)}{(y-t)^2}\right)\\
\end{align}</math>
|All of the other Painlevé transcendents are degenerations of the sixth
|<ref name=":2" />
|-
|[[Rabinovich–Fabrikant equations]]
|1
|<math>\begin{align}
\dot{x} &= y (z - 1 + x^2) + \gamma x \\
\dot{y} &= x (3z + 1 - x^2) + \gamma y \\
\dot{z} &= -2z (\alpha + xy)
\end{align}</math>
|[[Chaos theory]], [[dynamical system]]s
|<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rabinovich |first1=M. I. |last2=Fabrikant |first2=A. L. |date=1979-08-01 |title=Stochastic wave self-modulation in nonequilibrium media |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1979ZhETF..77..617R |journal=Zhurnal Eksperimentalnoi I Teoreticheskoi Fiziki |volume=77 |pages=617–629 |bibcode=1979ZhETF..77..617R |issn=0044-4510}}</ref>
|-
|[[Riccati equation]]
|1
|<math>\frac{dy}{dx} + Q(x) y + R(x) y^2 = P(x)</math>
|Class of first order differential equations that is quadratic in the unknown. Can reduce to [[Bernoulli differential equation]] or linear differential equation in certain cases
|<ref>{{Cite web |title=Riccati equation - Encyclopedia of Mathematics |url=https://encyclopediaofmath.org/index.php?title=Riccati_equation |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=encyclopediaofmath.org}}</ref>
|-
|[[Rössler attractor]]
|1
|<math>\begin{align}  \frac{dx}{dt} &= -y - z \\ \frac{dy}{dt} &= x + ay \\ \frac{dz}{dt} &= b + z(x-c) \end{align}</math>
|[[Chaos theory]], [[dynamical system]]s
|<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Peitgen | first1 = Heinz-Otto | author1-link = Heinz-Otto Peitgen
 | last2 = Jürgens | first2 = Hartmut | author2-link = Hartmut Jürgens
 | last3 = Saupe | first3 = Dietmar | author3-link = Dietmar Saupe

 | pages = 636–646
 | publisher = Springer

|}
